description:
FILED s461ar as the deliberate residue of #900, with the matrix measured.

#900 shipped perl's AUTOGENERATION (`++` from `+`, `--` from `-`, `+=`/`-=`
from both, object preserved).  What it did NOT ship is perl's refusal, because
`*p-overload-fallback*` is WRITTEN by p-register-overloads and read NOWHERE in
the runtime -- PCL ignores the flag entirely.  Measured 5.40.3, one class per
row, `$x++` / `$x--` / `$x += 2` on a blessed object:

    class overloads              fallback     perl                   PCL
    0+ "" +                      1            autogenerates          same (#900)
    0+ "" +                      (absent)     autogenerates          same (#900)
    0+ "" +                      0            DIES                   numifies
    0+ ""                        0            DIES                   numifies
    0+ ""                        (absent)     DIES                   numifies
    0+ ""                        1            uses the REF ADDRESS   uses 0+

perl's message is `Operation "++": no method found, argument in overloaded
package C`.  Note the LAST row, which is the surprising one and was probed
twice: with `fallback => 1` and no `+`/`++` handler, perl does NOT consult `0+`
for `++` -- it increments the reference ADDRESS (110257620425689 for a fresh
object).  PCL answers `0+` + 1 there, which is friendlier and wrong.

WHY IT WAS HELD BACK: a new DEATH in a path that today limps along needs its
own sweep + companion evidence, and `fallback => 1` is extremely common in real
CPAN classes, so the blast radius is not obvious from the matrix.  The
implementation is small -- %p-incdec-overload already has the two-value shape
and knows when NEITHER handler applies; the missing piece is reading
*p-overload-fallback* (with @ISA inheritance, like p-find-overload) and dying
unless it says T.

BAR: the six-row matrix above vs perl; full sweep; the op/ and uni/ companion
legs (overload-heavy); Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t's #900 rows extended.

=== SHIPPED s462at (agent AT, round 19) -- the `++`/`--` half.  The BINARY half
=== and the `fallback => 1` row are measured and split out (#960, #961).

WHAT SHIPPED.
  * `%p-overload-fallback-of CLS` -- perl's flag as T / :NO / :UNDEF, inherited
    through @ISA exactly as a handler is.  THE FIRST READER of
    *p-overload-fallback* in the runtime's life.
  * `%p-isa-parent-names` -- the @ISA lookup, which was spelled out THREE
    times (%p-find-overload-mro, %p-class-overloaded-p and now the fallback
    walk).  One reading; the two existing walkers were routed through it.
  * `%p-incdec-autogen` -- %p-incdec-overload's tail, and perl's rule:
    a `+`/`-` handler autogenerates UNLESS fallback is :NO; a class that
    overloads nothing declines to the caller's ordinary numeric path; a
    `fallback => 1` class with nothing to autogenerate keeps PCL's `0+` answer
    (#961); everything else DIES `Operation "++": no method found, argument in
    overloaded package C`.  The message names the OBJECT's class, not the one
    that registered the handlers -- probed on a subclass.
  * THE RAW PATH.  `$x++` on an unboxable slot emits `(p-incf-raw $x)` and
    routed a blessed operand to `p-+`, so the refusal fired on ONE emission
    path.  `%define-compound-pair` now carries a supplied-p: NO delta is
    `$x++` (Parser2 emits exactly that spelling for it and nothing else), a
    delta is `$x += 1`, and the first routes to perl-increment/perl-decrement,
    which own the whole decision.  This also closes a #900 hole nobody had
    noticed: a class with its OWN `++` handler was numified on the raw path.
  * perl-increment's `0+` arm is now reached for exactly ONE overloaded shape
    (the #961 one); its comment says so.

THE MATRIX, RE-PROBED 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl (15 rows, 6 SAME before / 12 after):
every row of the task's table plus `--`, `+=`, a plain `+`, an own-`++`-with-
fallback-0 class, a `""`-only class, a `bool`-only class, an unblessed-class
control, and the message text.  The three that still differ are #960 (`$o + 2`
and `$o += 2`) and #961 (`fallback => 1`).

WHY THE BINARY HALF IS NOT HERE, per the DECIDED s461f caution.  perl's message
for `+` and `+=` is a DIFFERENT, three-line shape ("left argument in overloaded
package C, right argument has no overloaded magic"), so the two halves cannot
even share a formatter, and the site (`p-+`, reached from %p-compound-+-slow
too) covers `+`, `+=` and the raw `$s += $obj` twin at once -- a much wider
blast radius.  The exposure was scanned rather than guessed: cpan-tests/ +
lib/ + perl-tests/ hold 23 files that say `use overload` at all, 5 with
`fallback => 1`, 1 with another value, 17 with none.  That is the population
the death must be measured against.  Task #960.

BARS MET.  Full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18342 -> 18343 (the +1 is
#939's), drops 5 = census.  Gate-SET scan over both populations IDENTICAL (a
runtime-only change cannot move it, and it did not).  Guard
`Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t` 50 -> 52 -- one row per EMISSION PATH (the default and
PCL_OPT=none), seven claims each including the two negatives (`fb1++` must NOT
die, plain numbers and the magical string increment untouched), with three new
fixture modules (AoNoFb, AoFb0, AoNoFbKid) so the classes come from a MODULE
and the raw slot is really used.  Inverse-verified on a 4c354bc worktree: rows
51-52 fail there, the other 50 pass.


s463f (Fable merge review, 2026-09-01): MERGED to main as 6e6f191 (AT worktree rebased over 12eacb5; the two conflicts were the DECIDED/session-log tops, both sections kept).  Fable probes vs perl 5.40.3: #939 19-row file SAME (substr/vec/pos/$#a targets, hash/array element bases, list/scalar/boolean contexts, tr, !~, /g, for-alias, m// unmoved); #934 25-row file SAME except the E-class row (fallback=>1 with nothing to autogenerate: PCL small vs perl big) = #961, pre-existing and filed by AT; #940 11-row file SAME once the probe rows that are INVALID PERL were dropped (a declared sub followed by `/ 3, "\n"` is a perl syntax error too).  Status flipped from pending.

=== s464aw (round 22): the refusal shipped here KILLED a `nomethod' class,
=== and #972 fixed it in `%p-incdec-autogen'.

Probed 5.40.3:

    package A1; use overload q(0+)=>sub{7}, q("")=>sub{"A1"},
                             nomethod => sub { "NM[$_[3]]" };
    my $x = A1->new; $x++;
    perl:  the nomethod handler is called ONCE (op=`++', other=undef,
           swapped=`''), its RETURN VALUE IS DISCARDED, and $x still holds
           the same blessed object (ref($x) eq 'A1', "$x" eq 'A1')
    PCL (before #972):  DIES `Operation "++": no method found, argument in
           overloaded package A1'

The refusal is otherwise unchanged; a `nomethod' arm now sits between the
"not overloaded at all" decline and the `fallback => 1' arm (#961's), and
returns the ORIGINAL value with appliedp = t, which is perl's discard.

SEPARATELY: this task's shipped comment on `%p-incdec-overload''s OWN-handler
arm -- "a mutator whose return value is what the place receives" -- is WRONG
in its second half.  perl DISCARDS an own `++'/`--' handler's return too
(`use overload '++' => sub {"INCED"}': perl leaves the object, PCL stores
"INCED" and declasses it).  Measured both ways; task #1004.  Zero classes in
cpan-tests/ + lib/ + perl-tests/ + perl's t/ declare a `++' key, so the
corpus cannot measure that fix and its guard rows will be the bar.
subject: overload FALLBACK is recorded and never read: perl DIES on ++/--/+= that cannot autogenerate, PCL numifies
